segments.text: One pot, twenty minutes, ingredients you already have: tonight we are making a tomato
pasta that never fails.
You need half a kilo of dry spaghetti, two cans of chopped tomatoes, four
garlic cloves, olive oil, salt, and a little dried oregano.
Fill your biggest pot two-thirds with water, salt it well, and bring it to
a rolling boil before the pasta goes in.
While it heats, slice the garlic thin.
Thin slices cook gently; burnt garlic turns bitter, so keep the heat medium.
Warm three spoonfuls of olive oil in a wide pan, add the garlic, and
stir for about a minute until it smells sweet.
Pour in the tomatoes, add a teaspoon of salt and the oregano, and let
it bubble gently while the pasta cooks.
Drop the spaghetti into the boiling water and cook it about a minute less
than the packet says, so it stays firm.
Before you drain, scoop out a full mug of the pasta water.
That cloudy water is what makes the sauce silky.
Move the pasta straight into the pan with the sauce and toss everything together
for one minute over the heat.
If it looks dry, splash in some of the saved water, a little at
a time, until the sauce coats every strand.
Taste it before serving.
Add salt bit by bit until it tastes bright, then finish with a thread
of olive oil.
If you cook for one or two, the leftovers keep three to four days
in a sealed box in the fridge.
Reheat leftovers in a pan with a splash of water until steaming all the
way through, and eat them within those few days.
So that is the method to remember: salty water, gentle garlic, firm pasta, and
a mug of pasta water for the sauce.
If this helped, subscribe to the channel for more weeknight dinners.
See you next time.
